title: Tenant-safe exact prefix cache
problem_statement: Repeated long prompts need an exact prefill reuse path that never crosses execution identity or tenant sharing-domain boundaries.
result_disclosure: This admission records no benchmark result or performance claim; a later implementation must disclose the required cache-off and cache-on fallback comparisons.
rollback: Keep the experimental flag false by default; a later implementation rollback disables the flag and reverts cache metadata and scheduler integration together.

approval_answers.user_workload_bottleneck: Repeated long prompts need an exact prefill reuse path that does not cross tenant or execution identities.
approval_answers.semantic_class_rationale: Prefix reuse changes no token or model semantics when every identity, complete block, and lifetime check passes, so it remains a reference-class systems change.

existing_ir_expression.rationale: Existing paged KV ownership has no prefix-cache identity, sharing-domain, or immutable cache-lifecycle representation.

approval_answers.implementation_location_rationale: A future core runtime and scheduler addition is required because the cache must bind KV block ownership, admission, and exact fallback behavior.
approval_answers.error_or_distribution_contract: The reference-class contract requires behavioral parity, token parity, stable fallback, and lifetime/resource regression coverage; no approximation is admitted.
approval_answers.memory_and_operational_complexity: Cache metadata and pins must remain bounded by configured block and byte budgets; this admission makes no hot-path allocation claim.
approval_answers.fallback_and_rollback: With the flag false or on any identity or lifetime validation failure, use the current exact prefill path; rollback disables the flag and reverts the later implementation as one unit.
approval_answers.end_to_end_benefit_hypothesis: For same-domain exact prefix hits, avoiding already-computed prefill work is hypothesized to lower TTFT while miss behavior stays within the declared fallback comparison.
